transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-02
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Samir Patel (CTO, Aurora), Maya Rios (Lead ML Eng), Alex Chen (SRE), Lina Torres (PM)

Topics: POC scope, success criteria, TTFT vs TPOT, p95/p99 targets, benchmark plan, timelines, security/VPC considerations

---
00:00 Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. um quick agenda — define the SLOs for the POC, figure out workload sizing and benchmarks, and lock a timeline. Priya and I will lead technical questions.
00:18 Samir Patel: Thanks Jordan. We're mainly focused on chat and long-form summarization. Our product has a real-time assistant and a nightly batch summarizer.
00:30 Maya Rios: yeah, for the assistant we see median latencies that are fine but our p95 spikes during peak and it's killing UX. We want to set realistic SLOs and validate cost tradeoffs.
00:45 Priya Nair: Got it. Quick clarifying q — when you say p95 spikes, are you measuring TTFT or token-level?
00:52 Maya Rios: currently TTFT from our front-end to first token. so TTFT. But we also care about end-to-end response time for longer completions, which is TPOT-ish.
01:04 Jordan Lee: perfect. So we usually separate TTFT (time-to-first-token) and TPOT (time-to-problem/total? token?) _Total processing time per turn_. For POC we recommend measuring both because batching and kv-cache behavior trades off differently.
01:20 Samir Patel: we want p95 < 300ms for short assistant replies (under 256 tokens) and p99 under 600ms ideally. Are those realistic?
01:31 Priya Nair: those are aggressive but possibly achievable on Dedicated with proper quantization and small context models. On Hosted you'll probably see higher p99 unless you use reserved capacity. We should scope by QPS and payload size first.
01:45 Alex Chen: our baseline is ~200 QPS during peak, 95% of requests < 192 tokens, 5% are long ~512 tokens. Nightly batch is ~10k docs but not latency sensitive.
01:59 Jordan Lee: good detail. For the POC we'll focus on the real-time assistant traffic shape. So measurement plan: define traffic profile (QPS, token distribution), create a benchmark harness that simulates front-end TTFT measurement, and run tests against Hosted (burst) and Dedicated/VPC.
02:16 Maya Rios: what about measuring token emission patterns? Some of our prompts stream tokens slowly and that affects perceived latency.
02:24 Priya Nair: yep include streaming scenarios. We'll measure TTFT and also time to 50% tokens and TPOT for full completion. We'll report p50/p95/p99 for both TTFT and TPOT.
02:36 Samir Patel: okay target table — TTFT p95 300ms, TTFT p99 600ms; TPOT p95 under 1.2s for short responses, TPOT p99 under 2.5s. Are those reasonable starting SLOs?
02:50 Priya Nair: reasonable as targets, but we'll caveat: TPOT for long completions scales with tokens and batching; the more batching the better cost but worse tail latency for single-turn low-latency needs. We'll model several batching configs.
03:06 Jordan Lee: also routing policy: you can route low-latency traffic to Dedicated and cost-sensitive to Hosted or lower-tier models. For POC we can run traffic split experiments.
03:18 Alex Chen: security — we need VPC peering, KMS for keys, and SOC2 documentation. Also data retention: no logs persisted beyond session for PII.
03:30 Jordan Lee: we'll attach the security pack. Redwood supports customer-managed KMS and VPC private deployments; SE will send network diagram and required firewall ports.
03:41 Samir Patel: notable competitors we tested earlier were Anthropic and OpenAI but we want to validate Redwood on cost and latency.
03:49 Priya Nair: noted. For measurement specifics, Priya: what's the harness look like?
03:55 Priya Nair: we'll provide a JMeter/locust-style harness plus a small Python harness that measures TTFT from a synthetic browser client (chrome-headless style). The harness will: 1) replay sample prompts, 2) measure TTFT, token emission times, and TPOT, 3) collect p50/p95/p99 and per-route breakdowns. We'll also instrument KV cache warm and cold scenarios.
04:20 Maya Rios: KV cache is important — most of our assistant traffic hits similar contexts so cold vs warm cache will be big. Can you measure both?
04:27 Priya Nair: yes — we'll run warm-runs after an initial warm-up and cold-run tests as well. We'll include prefix caching scenarios.
04:35 Samir Patel: timeline question — how long to run each configuration for statistically significant p99?
04:41 Priya Nair: typically you want sustained runs for 5-10 minutes per config at steady QPS to get stable p99; for very tight confidence we can do multiple runs. For the POC week we propose daily runs across model/quantization/batching permutations.
04:58 Jordan Lee: So proposed POC plan: week 1 — configure harness and get sample payloads; week 2 — run hosted and dedicated benchmarks; week 3 — analyze and tune (batching/quant); week 4 — report and decision. Does that align?
05:14 Samir Patel: yes, that aligns with our Q4 rollout. We'd like a 4-week POC.
05:20 Maya Rios: cost modeling — can you output token cost per 1M tokens and cost-per-1k requests for each config?
05:26 Jordan Lee: yes we'll include cost per config and tradeoffs. Expect to show throughput per GPU node, tokens/sec, and cost per 1M tokens across quant levels.
05:36 Alex Chen: for on-prem/VPC testing we need to supply a small cluster and we'll need a contact to coordinate install.
05:42 Priya Nair: I'll be the SE contact for installs; we'll provide an install runbook and a config manifest.
05:48 Lina Torres: success criteria from product side — if we can keep TTFT p95 under 300ms for 95% of traffic and reduce p99 by at least 30% vs baseline, we consider it a success.
06:02 Samir Patel: add stakeholder alignment: we need exec buy-in if cost is within 20% of our current spend.
06:09 Jordan Lee: noted. We'll include a cost target in the proposal.
06:15 Maya Rios: measurement quirks — front-end retries and network jitter affect observed TTFT. How do you handle that?
06:23 Priya Nair: measurement harness will run inside the same VPC when possible to reduce network variance, and we'll also run synthetic browser tests from real edge locations to capture client-side jitter. We'll flag any noisy samples.
06:36 Jordan Lee: any legal/procurement blockers we should know of?
06:40 Samir Patel: procurement wants a standard MSA and data processing addendum. We can share templates.
06:46 Jordan Lee: I'll send contract templates with the POC quote.
06:50 Maya Rios: one more technical — quantization levels: do you have recommended profiles for 8-bit vs 4-bit for our model family?
06:58 Priya Nair: we'll recommend a set: fp16 baseline, q8_default, q4_0 for aggressive cost savings. We'll include accuracy delta measurements vs our evaluation prompts.
07:12 Samir Patel: accuracy regressions: we need to ensure quality is within a 2% drop on our eval set.
07:18 Priya Nair: we will run the eval suite alongside latency tests and surface quality vs cost charts.
07:25 Jordan Lee: ok let's recap real quick. Priya, measurement plan will define TTFT and TPOT, warm/cold cache, streaming, p50/p95/p99. Customer to provide QPS distribution and sample prompts. Redwood to run Hosted and Dedicated tests, produce cost/latency/quality tradeoff report. Action items assigned.
07:48 Samir Patel: perfect. Anything else?
07:51 Alex Chen: please include required firewall ports and peering steps in the network doc.
07:55 Priya Nair: will do.
07:57 Jordan Lee: great, we'll follow up with timeline and POC statement of work. Thanks everyone.
08:03 Maya Rios: thanks.
08:05 Samir Patel: thanks all.

---
Questions captured:
- Do p95/p99 targets change between Hosted and Dedicated? (answered: yes, Dedicated more stable)
- Can Redwood run warm and cold cache scenarios? (answered: yes)

References / artifacts mentioned:
- Redwood POC proposal (link: https://redwood.example.com/proposals/aurora-poc)
- Measurement plan template (link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/poc-harness)
- Benchmark spreadsheet (link: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/aurora-bench)
- Security pack (SOC2, KMS, network guide) attached by Jordan

Recap / next steps:
- Jordan to send POC proposal and contracts; Priya to share measurement harness and plan; Aurora to provide sample payloads and QPS distribution; schedule benchmark week starting 2026-10-16.
